html:
Argan oil is pressed from the kernels of the fruit of the argan tree, which grows wild almost only in southwestern Morocco. Berber women of the Souss have made it by hand for centuries, for cooking and for the skin.

The work is slow: the nuts are cracked between stones and the kernels ground by hand. Goats climb the trees to eat the fruit, a famous sight. The argan forest, which holds the soil against the desert, became a UNESCO biosphere reserve in 1998.

From the 1990s demand for the oil in cosmetics grew around the world. Women's cooperatives were set up to sell it, giving many rural Berber women their own income. The know-how was listed by UNESCO in 2014. See also Morocco and couscous.
